text:
cheng: Heads-up — seeing ~15% tail latency increase on gRPC ingress after the framer change. Repro on canary. Quick perf shows extra work in the parse/coalesce path and a lot of memcpy churn.
rita: Which framer change exactly? the small-frame -> proto-unpack rewrite?
sam: Is this observed on HTTP/2 path too or only gRPC?
cheng: It's primarily gRPC. HTTP/2 uses the slim parser and is mostly stable. The new proto-unpack introduced a safe-copy step to avoid lifetime issues; microtrace shows ingress->proto_unmarshal->coalesce->memmove->tokenize. Small requests (<=256B) get de-chunked then reassembled which blows up CPU. Example perf dump I captured: 
```
perf top (sampled):
  ingress.parse_loop   38%
  grpc.readv_coalesce  22%
  tokenizer            15%
  memmove              12%
  kvcache.lookup       6%
  other                7%
```
rita: Oof. That memmove line is worrying. Did kvcache evictions spike as well? Could be churn exposing cold-shard lookups.
maria: Can you paste a pprof stack or a short flame view? Also what traffic shape (payload size distribution)?
cheng: pprof top from a 30s canary run: 
```
# pprof top
ingress.parseLoop       120ms
proto.coalesce           90ms
memmove.copy             45ms
tokenizer.tokenize       30ms
kvcache.lookup           10ms
```
Traffic: 70% requests are tiny (avg payload 180B), lots of multiplexed streams.
perf-bot: Alert: canary slope > 10% on p50->p95. Trace: https://perf.redwood/trace/1762349999
sam: Sounds like we need to avoid the extra copy for tiny frames. Two quick ideas: 1) increase readv vector size to reduce tiny fragments, 2) short-circuit safe-copy for frames below threshold and ensure buffer lifetime.
rita: Another option: push tokenization into a preparse sidecar worker for gRPC ingress (async pre-tokenize). That reduced host CPU in a prior experiment where we offloaded parse on a sidecar. Tradeoffs: latency for first token and added IPC.
maria: If we disable safe-copy for small frames we must add unit tests around buffer ownership, and run ASAN in CI for a bit. Also check kvcache hit-rate — if copies cause rehash jitter maybe evictions increased.
cheng: Plan for today: 1) bench readv vec=8 vs vec=32 vs vec=64 to see coalescing effect, 2) add a flag to skip safe-copy for frames <= 512B (with strict lifetime assertions in debug builds), 3) capture kvcache eviction counters during canary. I'll run a small canary patch with these toggles.
sam: Also consider write-side coalescing (MSG_MORE / writev) for outgoing streaming chunking to reduce number of small writes that force more reads on the other side.
cheng: Agreed. Will try readv tuning + safe-copy short-circuit first. If no win, we'll prototype sidecar pretokenize. I'll post bench numbers here.
maria: For the canary add an additional tracepoint around kvcache.lookup to correlate CPU spikes with miss rate.
deploy-bot: Canary deployed: framer-readv-experiment -> canary-3 (owner: cheng). Watch /deploys for rollback.
sam: :thumbsup:
rita: TY — will review the quick patch when you post it.
cheng: Posting bench results in ~1h.
